title: How your phone fakes that blurry portrait background
description: Phone lenses are too small for real background blur, so portrait mode simulates it using a depth map and software.

scenes.big: Your phone's blur is mostly software
scenes.say: Portrait mode looks like a pro camera. But a phone lens is tiny, so nearly everything is in focus.
Real background blur needs a large lens opening. A phone's aperture is small and fixed, so the blur gets simulated in software.

steps: A neural network outlines the person
Blur more the farther away it is
scenes.say: Google's Pixel 2 pipeline is a good example. A network masks the person. The camera estimates depth from the slight difference between two halves of each sensor pixel. Then background pixels are blurred in proportion to distance.

Because it's software, the blur can be any shape. The catch is that blank walls and repeating patterns can confuse the depth estimate, and the mask can miss unusual subjects. That's when edges look odd.
So lens blur is optics. Phone blur is math. Both can look great, and one fits in your pocket. Follow for more.
